body: @creationix Are you saying that after running this, you don't have `.eslintrc.js` (since you selected JavaScript format, file will have .js extension) file created in your `www` directory? Would you mind trying the same exact thing but with a `--debug` flag? As in `eslint --init --debug` it should provide some additional information. If you could post the result here, it would help us debug this problem.

https://asciinema.org/a/4g9lhuvch583q6mbe5w4mctz0

edit: Including text output in case asciinema goes down.

```
➜  sample-app git:(master) eslint --init                              
? How would you like to configure ESLint? Answer questions about your style
? Are you using ECMAScript 6 features? Yes
? Are you using ES6 modules? No
? Where will your code run? Browser
? Do you use CommonJS? No
? Do you use JSX? No
? What style of indentation do you use? Spaces
? What quotes do you use for strings? Single
? What line endings do you use? Unix
? Do you require semicolons? Yes
? What format do you want your config file to be in? JavaScript
➜  sample-app git:(master) ls -a                                    
.    ..   .git
➜  sample-app git:(master)                                            
```

Hmm.. Ok, that's very strange. Could you try it with `--debug` it might give us insight into what happened and why the file wasn't created. I have a feeling that I know what happened, but want independant confirmation anyways.

I'm able to reproduce this linked from latest `master`. Not sure what's going on. Neither `--debug` nor `DEBUG=eslint:all` produce any output. It's failing inside `processAnswers` with two errors:
- `TypeError: Cannot read property 'forEach' of undefined`
- `TypeError: Cannot read property 'plugins' of undefined`
Oh, that's not what I expected at all. I thought that the changes that we made to `config-file` would output config into location of global eslint installation.
It seems `inquirer` may have been swallowing errors, which is why we weren't getting stack traces before.
Yes, it does unless you call the callback with the errors.  It's kind of annoying to work with inquirer, honestly.   I think I know what's going on, gimme a few min to dig deeper.
